anatomy.intro: One opposite leaf pair forms the stone-like body around a central cleft.

parts.function: A fleshy leaf holds water that can support the next pair.
parts.label: Thick leaf

parts.function: Fine spotting contributes to the stone-like appearance.
parts.label: Speckled surface

parts.function: The opening separates the opposing leaves and allows new growth to emerge.
parts.label: Central cleft

parts.function: The opposite leaves are joined at their lower base.
parts.label: Joined base

flowers.text: Flowers emerge from the cleft and resemble large daisies. SANBI describes the species’ fragrant blooms opening in mid-afternoon. The Royal Flush nursery listing gives conflicting golden and pink color descriptions.

growth.note: Follow the visible stage rather than a month-based schedule; wrinkling outer leaves during renewal does not alone call for watering.

stages.text: A compact pair forms the main visible plant.
stages.title: Hold a leaf pair

stages.text: The cleft opens around an emerging inner pair.
stages.title: Reveal new leaves

stages.text: Older leaves lose stored water and eventually dry as the new pair develops.
stages.title: Use the outer pair

habitat.text: Wild Pleiospilos nelii grows among sparse Karoo vegetation near South Africa’s Western and Eastern Cape boundary. Rounded speckled leaves blend with the surrounding stones. 'Royal Flush' is a cultivated pink-purple form of this compact mimicry plant, retaining the deep cleft and thick opposing leaves.

Pleiospilos nelii Royal Flush: one single stemless split-rock plant, exactly TWO thick purple-mauve egg-shaped leaves forming ONE opposite leaf pair, joined at their low base, deep central cleft and fine dark speckles over the surfaces. Three-quarter close view, a few loose ground pebbles, leave lower joined base clearly visible. No inner new leaves at all, no flowers. Four numbered leaders: 1 points to the broad thick left leaf, 2 points to speckles on upper right leaf, 3 points into the central fissure between the pair, 4 points to the low joined base where the two leaves meet just above the soil. No stacked leaf pairs, no Lithops window patterns. Precisely two leaves, balanced natural anatomy.

lookalikes.name: Green split rock
lookalikes.text: The green split rock has the same thick, speckled leaf-pair structure, with grey-green coloring compared with Royal Flush’s pink-purple tones.

mature.text: The nursery lists roughly 3–5 inches high and 3–4 inches across. The body stays compact as one leaf generation gradually replaces another.

nameStory.text: Pleiospilos refers to its many spots. The species' woody seed capsules open when wet, letting raindrops release some seeds before the capsules close again as they dry.
